title: Starshine in Canis Major
caption: The Tau Canis Majoris Cluster, NGC 2362, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 2362, Tau Canis Majoris · constellation Canis Major · about 5000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: One star dominates the centre of this ESO picture: Tau Canis Majoris, a massive multiple star system that outshines every other member of its home cluster, NGC 2362, in Canis Major, the Great Dog. Around it are many fainter young stars, only four or five million years old and just starting their lives.

NGC 2362, often named after that bright star, is an open cluster whose stars all emerged from one molecular cloud. Its members share a chemical make-up and are loosely held together by gravity. Having been born together, they form an ideal laboratory for testing ideas about stellar evolution, the sequence from a star's birth in a cool, dense cloud to its death.

Although these stars formed at the same time, their different masses will send them down very different paths. Tau Canis Majoris belongs to one of the most massive, short-lived types of star, so it will use up its fuel long before its smaller neighbours, which will keep shining for billions of years.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.37 x 7.47 arcminutes) and distance (5000 light years), the frame spans roughly 11 × 11 light-years. Its light set out about 5,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The FORS2 instrument on the Very Large Telescope imaged the cluster through blue, visual and red filters in visible light. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
filters: 440 nm · Optical b (Very Large Telescope FORS2)

understand.eye: The camera's exposure gathers far more light than the eye, revealing many faint young stars around the bright central system.

explore: The image was made for the ESO Cosmic Gems programme, which uses telescope time unsuitable for science to create images for education and outreach. Its data are still archived for astronomers. The cluster lies about 5000 light-years away.
alt: A very bright star at the centre of a cluster of fainter stars.
